text:
alex: quick flagging - noticed p95 dashboard latency climbed ~30ms last week. traced to large auth calls inside the query fanout. want to discuss an alternate surface: 'auth projections' that the gateway can attach to queries to let services pre-filter rows/columns before heavy joins.

nora: 'auth projections' sounds promising. are you thinking of a tiny projection RPC that returns compiled row-filters + allowed-columns per subject+resource?

alex: yes. instead of evaluating full policy in every downstream service, compute a compact projection once per request (or cached per subject+resource), then downstream applies it as a DB-level predicate. avoids N auth calls per widget.

pranav: two immediate tradeoffs: 1) correctness window if projection is stale; 2) explosion of projection variants (roles, seat levels, dataset scopes). both affect cache hit rates.

jen: proposal sketch: projection service with these properties: versioned proto, ETagable, TTL, conservative-by-default semantics. example contract: 
```
POST /v1/projections/batch
body: { checks: [{subject: "user:42", resource: "dash:9001", context: {seats:["s:5"]}}, ...] }
resp: { results: [{etag: "v12", columns: ["col_a","col_b"], row_pred_sql: "tenant_id = 42 AND status != 'archived'"}, ...] }
```
downstream uses etag as cache key; if missing or mismatch, falls back to full policy call synchronously.

nora: how do we ensure we don't under-restrict? i prefer the projection service always err-on-deny (i.e., filter stricter than policy) and include a permissive-hint flag for sampled double-checks.

pranav: err-on-deny increases false-deny surface — could break dashboards. we need a gradual migration: run in 'audit' mode that attaches projection but still executes full-policy for sampled requests to compute divergence. create divergence metric and abort rollout if >0.2% over 24h.

sasha: instrumentation notes: emit metrics: projection.latency_ms, projection.cache_hit_rate, projection.divergence.count, projection.size_bytes. add a dashboard for correlation: projection.divergence vs render-failure-rate.

jen: ops considerations: projection service should be horizontally scalable, single-digit ms median, p95 target <25ms. batch call support critical. also rate-limit by tenant to avoid noisy neighbors. think small CPU instances with large TLS connection pools.

alex: API placement options: A) gateway calls projection before fanout and attaches projection metadata to each downstream request. B) downstream services call projection themselves and cache results. pros/cons?

nora: A centralizes logic and measurement, easier to enforce TTLs and batching. B reduces central dependency but increases duplicated projection logic. prefer A for initial rollout.

pranav: rollout: 1) implement projection service + batch endpoint behind flag but in audit mode; 2) gateway attaches projections but downstream still runs full-policy; 3) enable sampled divergence checks (start 5% -> 1%); 4) after 2 weeks and divergence <0.2%, flip to enforce for single-tenant dashboards only. add kill-switch.

jen: add migration checklist: metadata versioning policy, cache eviction hooks (on role change, seat revoke, resource update), and a fast path for explicit invalidation via write hooks. also consider tombstone semantics for deleted resources.

sasha: alerts: projection.divergence.rate > 0.2% sustained 1h; projection.latency.p95 > 50ms; projection.error_rate > 0.5% per tenant. Ops playbook: revert gateway flag, roll back projection instances.

alex: owners: alex (arch + gateway integration), nora (projection design + policy semantics), jen (ops + infra), pranav (auth correctness + monitoring), sasha (telemetry). i'll draft a short RFC with contract, metrics, and test plan.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staged branch 'projection-proto' queued to staging canary. estimated finish: ~25m.

jen: once canary is up i'll run synthetic load: 500 concurrent dash renders with mixed fanout and measure render success and latency.

pranav: one more thought: for multi-tenant shared widgets we might need compositional projections (per-embed resource). start scope: single-tenant dashboards + widgets owned by tenant. avoid cross-tenant widgets in first phase.

alex: agreed. draft RFC will include scope, sample payloads, and measurement dashboards. meeting next Tue to review API and rollout steps.

jen: thanks all, excited to reduce that auth tail. :rocket:
